Hi Sam / Acme onboarding team,

Thanks for choosing Redwood for your private deployment. I wanted to kick off the network & environment onboarding work so we can lock the Day-0 checklist and schedule a short walk-through. Below is a compact preflight Im asking you to confirm ahead of the call. If you prefer, Ben or Kim can run through these during a 30-minute session.

Quick asks (please reply inline):
- Primary technical contact + backup (name, phone, preferred Slack/Teams handle)
- Target CIDR for host subnets and any reserved ranges we should avoid
- Egress model: do you need fixed public egress IPs (for allowlisting) or will you use NAT gateway per-AZ?
- Interconnect type: VPN or dedicated circuit (ExpressRoute/Interconnect)? Provide circuit ID / peering contact if applicable.
- TLS termination: will Acme manage public certs (ACME) or want Redwood to terminate internally?
- KMS: customer-managed key required? Provide KMS ARN or HSM vendor details.
- Service account / roles: who will own the service account (we attach a template)
- Firewall / allowlist: outbound ports we must open (default list included below)
- Test window: preferred date/time (MST) for smoke traffic and cert validation

Minimum network ports we will exercise during smoke tests:
- 443 (HTTPS outbound to Redwood control plane endpoints)
- 5222/5671 (if you use internal ingest pipelines over TLS)
- 5228-5230 (agent control plane heartbeats, optional)

Attachments: Im attached our onboarding prereqs PDF and an example access-roles YAML to speed role creation.

Wem aiming to have environment validation (DNS, routing, KMS, certificates, and a 5-minute smoke request) completed within 48 hours of the walk-through. If there are regulatory constraints (air-gap / no internet egress), call that out and wem provide an alternate offline activation path.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes

Sam —

Quick answers to your clarifying Qs and some operational notes: 

1) Fixed egress IPs: We can support either model. For smallest blast radius and simplest allowlisting, we typically provide a pair of static egress IPs per-tenant (active/passive) per-region. If you need a single IP, we can gate the control-plane traffic through a NAT with a single EIP, but that creates single-point-of-failure unless paired across zones. Let us know preference.

2) Installer ENI permissions: optional but recommended. If youm doing a managed on-prem or VPC deploy where our runtime needs direct hooks (metrics collection, health checks), the service-account needs IAM permissions to create/describe ENIs, attach/detach, and read tags. The roles template we attached includes a minimal policy.

Operational checklist highlights (we will expand during the walk):
- DNS: CNAME pointing to Redwood control-plane ingress (provide name and TTL)
- Certs: PEM chain and private key delivered via secure Artifact (we accept signed S3 presigned or sftp)
- KMS: policy granting decrypt & generate-data-key permission to the service principal (we provide exact ARN in the audit doc)
- Time sync: NTP access outbound to pool.ntp.org (or provide internal NTP IP)
- Monitoring: outbound to our metrics endpoint on 443 and to your Datadog endpoint if you want local forwarding

Im attaching a brief example access-roles YAML that maps to the minimal permissions we need. If you want, Kim and I can join the Tuesday slot to run the smoke test.

Ben Carter
Senior Onboarding Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
